races.name: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Fillies Maiden
Saudi Cup Silver Flash Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Alpha
runners_data.note: Won impressively over 7f on good ground last time, handled soft before that — course and conditions suit; Ryan Moore's positional intelligence gives him an edge tracking Blonde Over Blue and striking at the right moment.

runners_data.name: Alpine Wedding
runners_data.note: Placed twice in similar-going conditions at 7f — consistent without winning; W J Lee likely to have him close to the pace but the 4-day turnaround after a run is worth monitoring for freshness.

runners_data.name: Blonde Over Blue
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner and likely to control the race from the gates; her natural lead role is confirmed and unchallenged here — the key question is whether she retains enough to hold off prominent chasers late on this flat 7½f.

runners_data.name: Cedrela
runners_data.note: Wholly unexposed with no historical data available — the Colin Keane booking and a De Aguiar yard that has used its runners sparingly are the only clues; must be treated as a wildcard with unknown pace profile and going suitability.

runners_data.name: Dancing Destiny
runners_data.note: Has won twice and shown consistent form at distances up to 8f on good ground, but her front-running instincts will be frustrated here — with Alpha, Alpine Wedding and Blonde Over Blue all forward, she is likely to find herself racing in a position further back than she finds comfortable.

runners_data.name: Green Empress
runners_data.note: Two second-place finishes at 6f on good ground suggest she handles conditions well; stepping up to 7½f for the first time is the key unknown, and Dylan Browne McMonagle will need to decide whether to push for cover or ride her more prominently than usual given her style uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Nevermindtherain
runners_data.note: Form figures of 3-5-5 at 5-7f suggest she is struggling to land a blow at this level; Wayne Lordan rides and her hold-up tag suits a race with a strong pace, but the limited ceiling shown in recent outings makes it hard to be optimistic.

runners_data.name: Tosca No Candis
runners_data.note: Back-to-back fifth-place finishes at 7-8f on good ground — has not beaten a single rival home across two starts; hold-up style requires a strong pace and a clear run, neither of which is guaranteed in a field with limited true pace.

races.paceDynamic: Blonde Over Blue is the one confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field and, with no genuine speed rival to push her, she is set to bowl along at a sustainable, self-controlled tempo over Leopardstown's flat 7½f. Alpha and Alpine Wedding are natural prominent racers who will track close to the pace, meaning the early stages will not be truly soft, but equally there is nothing to force Blonde Over Blue into an unsustainable gallop. The field contains more prominent-type horses than the race shape can comfortably accommodate — Dancing Destiny is a genuine press-from-the-front type who will be squeezed back into a midfield role she does not naturally prefer, blunting her chance. A controlled, honest pace over good ground on a flat track favours horses who can travel prominently in behind the leader and produce a clean, sustained finish — the prominent-to-handy profile, particularly those with proven form at 7f on good ground, holds the clearest tactical advantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Blonde Over Blue Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Blonde Over Blue is allowed to dictate a measured pace and the prominent trackers cannot quicken past her inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Blonde Over Blue leads from the gates, sets a fair but unthreatening gallop, and has enough left in the tank to fend off challenges late on this flat track; Alpha and Alpine Wedding, travelling prominently, are best placed to mount the closest challenges but face a wall of a horse who has not been pressured.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Strike Late
scenarios.trigger: If Alpha or Alpine Wedding travel smoothly just off Blonde Over Blue's shoulder and kick decisively once daylight opens in the final 2f.
scenarios.body: The pace set by Blonde Over Blue proves genuine enough to string the field out but not so fast as to exhaust the chasers, and the horses tracking closest inherit the momentum to sweep past; Alpha's 7f win on good going and Ryan Moore's positional intelligence make him the most dangerous in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Unexposed Type Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lightly raced or unexposed runners — Green Empress or Cedrela — show previously unseen pace and class over this step up to 7½f.
scenarios.body: Green Empress has posted two solid runner-up efforts at 6f on good ground and could find the extra distance unlocking a new dimension; Cedrela is wholly unknown but connections and Colin Keane's booking suggest significant stable confidence, and a well-run race at this trip might expose her ceiling.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final furlong after a falsely run race and hold-up horses Nevermindtherain or Tosca No Candis come from off the pace.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires both a relatively quick early tempo to soften the leaders and a clean run through traffic for the back-markers, conditions that look unlikely given Blonde Over Blue's proven ability to control proceedings; Nevermindtherain has shown only modest form at lower weights and Tosca No Candis has failed to beat a rival home in two starts, making this shape the least likely.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Dancing Destiny attempts to push forward from the gates — if she contests the early positions with Blonde Over Blue rather than settling back, it could inject unexpected pace and destabilise the front-runner's control.

Cedrela is entirely unexposed and Colin Keane takes the ride for a stable running at a low strike-rate — an unknown profile over 7½f on debut conditions could produce a significant performance in either direction.

Green Empress steps up from 6f to 7½f for the first time — if Dylan Browne McMonagle elects to push forward rather than settle her in, her true ceiling at this trip will be tested sharply against more seasoned 7f rivals.

Monitor whether the early tempo set by Blonde Over Blue is genuinely honest — if Moore on Alpha or Lee on Alpine Wedding push up to pressure her in the opening 3f, the race shape shifts materially toward hold-up horses getting into the race late.

races.name: Japan Racing Association Tyros Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Aix La Chapelle
runners_data.note: Won on debut over 7f on Good ground at Leopardstown — exact course, distance, and going repeat — making this Ryan Moore-ridden O'Brien juvenile the prime beneficiary of a clean prominent pitch behind an uncontested front-runner; 50 days off is the one minor query but connections clearly targeted this race.|

runners_data.name: Florida Bay
runners_data.note: Three runs of solid form including a 7f win on Good, but the crowded prominent berth means she is likely to find herself slightly further back than ideal — her chance is real if she breaks smartly, but the style-fit tag is an honest caveat that this race shape may not serve her as well as a less congested field would.|

runners_data.name: Folsom Blues
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's promising prominent racer won over 7f on Soft and placed over 6f on Good, so the step back to 7½f on Good is a genuine question about whether he recaptures his best; Dylan Browne McMonagle takes over and will look to slot in just off Nail House's back.|

runners_data.name: Nail House
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner in a six-runner field, with a win over 6f on Good and J M Sheridan booked; only 15 days since last run which is fine, and his primary risk is a modest pace that leaves too much to chase down in the straight rather than any going or stamina concern at this trip.|

runners_data.name: Supreme Lord
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with a single third-place finish over 6f on Good and a trainer running at 0/12 over 14 days — the unknown style (flagged U) makes positional reading impossible, and the step up in class to Group 3 against more exposed rivals demands a big uptick.|

runners_data.name: Tio Joao
runners_data.note: Completely unexposed with no recorded last-run data and an unknown going profile, mapped to hold-up because the field lacks true closers; W J Lee rides for the same yard as Supreme Lord, and until this runner produces evidence on the track its role in any scenario is speculative at best.|

races.paceDynamic: Nail House is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only six runners and no genuine pressure expected from the prominent trio, should be able to dictate a sustainable, metronomic gallop from the outset. Aix La Chapelle, Folsom Blues, and Florida Bay will all look to race prominently, but with three horses chasing one natural leader's early position, at least one of them will be racing marginally out of their comfort zone — Florida Bay is the most likely to find herself shuffled back rather than securing the rail or the slot she wants. This field holds more prominent types than the race shape can comfortably accommodate, meaning the positioning battle in the early stages will be subtle but consequential, with Nail House controlling the tempo from a position of unchallenged comfort. A controlled, front-end gallop on Good ground at Leopardstown over 7½f strongly favours horses who can sit close to or on the pace and quicken from a prominent position — confirmed prominents who can travel smoothly and produce a late kick, or the front-runner if the pace is genuinely sustainable, are the profiles to be on.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front-runner dictates cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Nail House bowls along uncontested and the prominent trio fail to apply meaningful pressure through the middle mile.
scenarios.body: Nail House sets an honest but controlled tempo, reaches the home turn with reserves intact, and kicks clear before rivals can organise a challenge; the 7½f trip on Good ground suits a horse that won over 6f and should see out the extra furlong comfortably with no pace to pull against.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent types overhaul leader
scenarios.trigger: If Aix La Chapelle or Folsom Blues tracks Nail House in a perfect position and produces a stronger finish in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: The front-runner's pace proves slightly too conservative to resist a well-positioned chaser who has been cantering on the bridle into the home straight; Good ground at Leopardstown rewards the horse with the superior turn of foot coming off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Messy pace, closers get in
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent types jostle for position and create a more pressured early gallop than expected, spreading the field and leaving the rear rank in contention.
scenarios.body: A fractious early pace compresses the field and provides a better surface for horses who have been held up; Supreme Lord or Tio Joao, though lightly raced and positionally uncertain, are handed an opportunity their raw ability might allow them to exploit.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Florida Bay recaptures form
scenarios.trigger: If Florida Bay does manage to secure a prominent pitch rather than being redistributed rearward, and her recent form figures mask residual quality.
scenarios.body: Despite being mapped back due to the congested prominent bracket, a clean early break could restore Florida Bay to her natural position just off the lead; if she travels like her win on the same going suggests she can, she re-enters the picture at a bigger price.

watchPoints.text: Nail House — if he bounces out and settles into an uncontested rhythm with no horse prepared to take him on, the race may effectively be over turning for home; watch whether any of the prominents attempt to close down the gap before the home bend.

Florida Bay — her draw and break from the stalls are the key early indicators; if she does not secure a forward pitch within the first two furlongs she is racing against her profile, and her chance should be downgraded accordingly in-running.

Aix La Chapelle — the 50-day absence following a debut win is the one unknowable in an otherwise compelling profile; watch for any signs of freshness or greenness under Moore in the early stages that might disrupt his positioning.

Supreme Lord and Tio Joao — both trained by Robson De Aguiar (0/12 over 14 days) and both lightly raced unknowns; if either shows unexpected pace or tactical versatility in the early stages it could alter the shape more than the form book anticipates.

Folsom Blues — his prior win came on Soft ground and his Good-ground form is placed but unproven over this trip; if the pace is genuinely compressed rather than strung out, his finishing kick over a shorter effective trip may be the sharpest weapon in the field behind the leader.

races.name: Dublin To Bahrain Race Series Handicap

runners_data.name: Apercu
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with consistent form around 10f on Good and similar ground (sim-going 11/15), won at Stanton two starts ago and placed repeatedly at this trip — W J Lee in the saddle adds confidence; best placed of the prominent quartet to track Mr Ballynonty cleanly.|

runners_data.name: Kilcrea Rock
runners_data.note: Last-time-out winner over 10f on Standard with Dylan Browne McMonagle up for Joseph O'Brien, who has been firing (19/58 in 14 days); 58-day absence is a mild flag, but the trainer's strike rate suggests the horse will be ready, and the return to Good suits.|

runners_data.name: Glyndwr
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose two recent wins came over 8f on Standard — stepping up to 1m1f on Good with Ben Coen needs a pace that strings the field; no headgear, trainer quiet at 0/4 in 14 days, but freshness (14-day return) could be a plus if the race sets up late.|

runners_data.name: Dark Viper
runners_data.note: A natural prominent-style racer who has won and placed repeatedly off the front end, but with four prominent types already competing for those positions this field shape is likely to push him back beyond his comfort zone — Shane Foley's handling of traffic will be key, though the style displacement is real.|

runners_data.name: Manton Bay
runners_data.note: Three-year-old who has placed at 10f on Good and won over 8f on Standard — Luke McAteer's claim helps at the weights, and the drop back from recent higher-grade efforts makes this more winnable; needs a clear run in what could be a bunched mid-race.|

runners_data.name: Wild Sapphire
runners_data.note: Won her most recent start over 8f on Good and has solid placed form at 8f-9f — D K Weld sends her back quickly (9 days) suggesting she's in form, but she naturally wants to race prominently and is likely to find herself shuffled into midfield given the traffic ahead of her, blunting her chance.|

runners_data.name: Harmani
runners_data.note: Won at 10f on Good two starts back for G M Lyons — Colin Keane takes over which is a significant jockey upgrade, and recent form over the right trip and going is encouraging; the 14-day turnaround is routine for this yard, and he has the tactical pace to sit handily.|

runners_data.name: Eastern Peace
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose sole win came on Standard over 10f — Good going and a field that may not truly string out are concerns, and the apprentice claim (Patrick McGettigan 5lb) may not compensate; needs a genuine pace collapse to get into this.|

runners_data.name: Mr Ballynonty
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner with no credible pace rival — trainer-ridden by Andrew Slattery who knows the horse intimately; runs in a hood (headgear) which may sharpen focus, and recent form shows consistency at this trip on Good, giving him every chance to dictate and hang on.|

races.paceDynamic: Mr Ballynonty is the sole confirmed front-runner and, crucially, faces no credible challenger for the lead — he should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset on Good ground over 1m1f at Leopardstown. Behind him, Apercu, Kilcrea Rock, Manton Bay and Harmani all want prominent positions, creating a congested battle for the four or five places directly behind the leader between the two- and three-furlong markers that will generate traffic issues and pocket risks. Glyndwr and Eastern Peace are the genuine hold-up horses who will be dropped in last or near-last and will need the field to string out to make their runs count. This field holds more prominent-leaning types than the race shape can accommodate — Dark Viper and Wild Sapphire are natural prominent racers who are highly unlikely to secure that berth and will find themselves racing further back than ideal, meaning their chances in a prominent-led shape are structurally compromised. The race shape strongly favours horses who can sit second or third off a lone, unhurried front-runner and quicken in the straight — a tactical, prominent-to-lead profile is the standout beneficiary.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Ranger Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Ballynonty dictates an unchallenged, even tempo and the prominent quartet can't close the gap early enough.
scenarios.body: Mr Ballynonty sets a soft, uncontested pace that allows him to conserve energy and sprint clear in the straight, denying the hold-up horses sufficient run-in. Horses who can sit close to him without expending excess energy early — Apercu and Kilcrea Rock — are ideally positioned to challenge and outfinish the field.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Resolves
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion sorts itself cleanly by halfway and a mid-pack stalker times a run to perfection.
scenarios.body: The jostling between Apercu, Kilcrea Rock, Manton Bay and Harmani produces a clear winner from that group who settles second or third and pounces smoothly from two furlongs out. Harmani's recent winning form on Good going at 10f and Manton Bay's course-applicable form make them the likeliest beneficiaries if they navigate the traffic without incident.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Strike
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group burns each other off and the pace quickens sharply enough to set up a late run.
scenarios.body: Glyndwr and Eastern Peace need the field to race freely and open ground to materialise from off the pace — a genuine stretch-out is required. Glyndwr's two recent wins came over shorter on Standard, so the extra furlong and Good ground are questions, but Glyndwr is the more likely beneficiary of the two if conditions set up late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Late
scenarios.trigger: If Mr Ballynonty goes too hard for his own good and folds inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: An overly ambitious pace from Mr Ballynonty would theoretically bring the deeper closers into play, but with only Eastern Peace and Glyndwr as true hold-up types and neither boasting convincing form on this trip and going combination, the scenario is structurally unlikely. Dark Viper and Wild Sapphire, though redistributed to midfield, lack the true hold-up profile to fully capitalise even if the pace collapses.

watchPoints.text: Mr Ballynonty's uncontested lead is the race's central dynamic — if he gets a soft time in front and is allowed to control fractions, the field behind him may never get close enough in the straight.

The four-way battle for prominent positions between Apercu, Kilcrea Rock, Manton Bay and Harmani at the 2-3 furlong mark creates significant pocket and traffic risk — any of these caught wide or blocked could be beaten before the straight opens up.

Wild Sapphire and Dark Viper, both natural prominent types, face a structural problem — watch where they actually settle at the start, as any compromise in position will significantly reduce their chance in the expected race shape.

Kilcrea Rock's 58-day absence is worth monitoring in the parade ring — Joseph O'Brien's 19/58 14-day record suggests intent, but a horse returning from nearly two months off into a congested prominent group warrants physical inspection.

Glyndwr and Eastern Peace will be the last to show — their finishing runs will reveal whether the pace was genuinely strong enough to set up late, making them useful race-shape reads regardless of their win prospects.

races.name: Dubai Racing Carnival Rated Race

runners_data.name: Wyman
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on Good last time and has course-relevant form — Shane Foley likely pushes forward from stall to claim the prominent position behind Handshake, which suits this horse's style, though a step up to 1m5f for the first time is an untested stamina question at OR 88 in a rated race.

runners_data.name: Handshake
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien's lightly raced three-year-old (single run, OR 120) is the class standout and has Dylan Browne McMonagle aboard — the 174-day absence is the key risk, but the horse's natural front-running style is ideally suited to this uncontested lead with no rival capable of applying pressure.

runners_data.name: Keepsgettingbetter
runners_data.note: Donnacha O'Brien's charge has genuine placing speed and a good recent form string including back-to-back wins — naturally a prominent racer, it is pushed toward midfield on the map because the field already has more pace-hungry types than available positions, and Gavin Ryan will likely find the front slots occupied, making its task harder than its style prefers.

runners_data.name: Lord Aus
runners_data.note: J P Murtagh's three-year-old is a proven hold-up performer who won over 12f on Good ground last time and steps up to 1m5f with that stamina evidence — Ben Coen rides and the 43-day break looks straightforward, making Lord Aus the most naturally suited horse to a slow-run race that develops late, if the class gap to Handshake can be bridged.

races.paceDynamic: Handshake is the one confirmed front-runner in this four-runner field and, with no credible challenger for the lead, Dylan Browne McMonagle can dictate an entirely uncontested, measured gallop over 1m5f on Good turf at Leopardstown. Wyman is the only other horse with a prominent profile but, at OR 88 against Handshake's OR 120, is unlikely to apply any meaningful pressure, meaning Handshake can roll along at a pace of his own choosing and conserve energy for the closing stages. Keepsgettingbetter is a genuine prominent type who has been redistributed to midfield on the map because there are more front-running/prominent types than positions to accommodate them — Handshake is most likely to secure that lead role with Wyman likely to fill the remaining prominent berth, leaving Keepsgettingbetter unable to race in its natural position. This controlled, single-pace scenario heavily favours a horse capable of tracking the steady fractions and producing a sustained gallop home — Lord Aus, a genuine hold-up type with a strong recent record at this trip on Good ground, is ideally profiled to finish strongly, while Handshake's ability to control every yard makes the front-running shape the dominant template.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Handshake Controls, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Handshake bowls along uncontested and the steady pace rewards the horse who can sustain it longest from the front.
scenarios.body: McMonagle takes Handshake to the front without contest, sets a comfortable gallop and kicks on turning for home, dictating every yard of the race; the slow-to-moderate tempo suits a horse of Handshake's class and fresh legs after 174 days off, and no rival has the pace to reel him in late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow enough that hold-up horses generate significant momentum off the turn and run past a tiring Handshake.
scenarios.body: Lord Aus, ridden by Ben Coen from the back, produces a sustained staying run on ground that suits (Good, 1m5f winner) and catches Handshake who has used himself up controlling the fractions; the 45-point OR advantage Handshake holds makes this unlikely, but Lord Aus's recent 12f win on Good is a live qualifier.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Quickens
scenarios.trigger: If Wyman or Keepsgettingbetter tracks Handshake closely and proves the classier finisher when the pace picks up in the straight.
scenarios.body: Shane Foley on Wyman, fresh off a recent win and prominent by nature, sits just behind Handshake and produces a sharp turn of foot in the straight to deny the pacesetter; Keepsgettingbetter's natural prominent style, compromised by redistribution, limits its effectiveness here but cannot be entirely dismissed given the small field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart
scenarios.trigger: If Handshake shows signs of rustiness after 174 days off and the race becomes a tactical lottery in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: With the controlling force compromised, the race degenerates into a sprint finish from a slow pace, favouring whichever jockey times the run best; Lord Aus and Wyman are the most likely beneficiaries in a scrambled finish, though this remains a low-probability outcome given Handshake's class.

watchPoints.text: Handshake's 174-day layoff is the single biggest risk factor — watch the paddock for any signs of condition and the early strides for whether McMonagle is happy to roll forward or shows reluctance.

If Wyman pushes forward aggressively at the start and applies any early pressure to Handshake, the pace could quicken slightly, compressing the advantage for Handshake and opening the door for Lord Aus's late run.

Keepsgettingbetter will likely be denied its natural position — watch whether Gavin Ryan accepts the midfield slot early or fights for position, as crowding in a four-runner field could still produce trouble in running.

Lord Aus was beaten 13 lengths in a soft-ground sprint over 8f but has since found his trip and ground — the reversion to Good and 12f-plus distances has transformed this horse, and the trend of his last two runs (win, win) is worth noting in the context of a small-field stamina test.

races.name: Turkish Jockey Club Handicap

runners_data.name: Friary Road
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who won over 16f on Good last time for trainer T M Walsh; likely to lead throughout over this 1m7f trip but STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence if pressed, and top weight of 142lbs is worth respecting late.

runners_data.name: Trubshaw
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead runner returning after 60 days off; won over 14f on Good and shapes as a natural prominent type who should slot in behind the leader, but the break may blunt his sharpness on debut for this yard.

runners_data.name: Party Dress
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who comes into this just eight days after her last run; best form on Good ground over 14f and she may appreciate the extra distance here, though fading finishes in soft suggest she needs things to set up for her.

runners_data.name: Tatum
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Noel Meade with strong recent form — placed in five of last seven — and a course-friendly profile on Good going over middle distances; at 135lbs she remains competitive off OR 65 and Paddy Harnett's 5lb claim is a useful ally.

runners_data.name: Jr Mahon
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse whose last six outings include finishes of 8th, 18th, and 14th — the form is poor and a 3-day turnaround is aggressive; going is fine but the distance and consistency concerns are real.

runners_data.name: Jurality
runners_data.note: The most consistent horse in the field with a form string of 532125 and five placed efforts at this level on Good ground; Paul Flynn's runner travels prominently and has the tactical versatility to sit just off a dawdling Friary Road and quicken late, making him a major player in the dominant shape.

runners_data.name: Miss Gitana
runners_data.note: A natural rear-of-field operator placed into midfield on the map because there are more hold-up types than the shape can absorb — she fades in finishes and her record of 9th, 13th, 8th, 9th and 16th on Good is uninspiring; trainer has 0 runners in the T14 window.

runners_data.name: Stone Rulya
runners_data.note: Tagged as fading in finishes and has not won or placed on turf in her last five recorded turf runs; Wesley Joyce's 3lb claim helps on the weight but this four-year-old's recent form does not inspire confidence over 1m7f on Good.

runners_data.name: Folly Beach
runners_data.note: Veteran eight-year-old whose natural style is hold-up but is shown in midfield due to redistribution — two wins on soft suggest she is not ideally suited to Good and her last win was over 13f in softer conditions; Jack Cleary's 5lb claim is the main angle but the profile is against her.

races.paceDynamic: Friary Road is the lone confirmed front-runner in a nine-runner field and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, is set to control the gallop from the front over this 1m7f trip at Leopardstown on Good turf. Trubshaw, Tatum, and Jurality will push forward into prominent positions behind the leader, creating a compact early order but not a pressured pace — Friary Road can dictate terms at a tempo of his own choosing. The hold-up brigade — Party Dress, Jr Mahon, Stone Rulya — will settle at the rear, while Miss Gitana and Folly Beach, both true hold-up types, have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field contains more horses wanting to race prominent than the shape can accommodate at the front; in reality Friary Road, Trubshaw, and Tatum are most likely to actually secure the forward positions. A sustainable, front-runner-controlled gallop over a long trip on Good ground historically favours horses who travel prominently and can quicken off a sound pace, making the prominent-to-midfield profile — horses like Jurality and Tatum — best placed to exploit the shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Friary Road Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Friary Road bowls along uncontested and sets a fair, even gallop that suits those tracking him.
scenarios.body: Friary Road dictates his own rhythm and the prominent horses travel comfortably in behind, setting up a steadily-run race that rewards those with enough class and stamina to quicken late; a consistent, honest pace over 1m7f on Good ground means the winner is likely to emerge from the lead or just off it.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Crumbles, Closers Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If Friary Road sets an overly generous gallop that collapses inside the final two furlongs, allowing rearward horses to close.
scenarios.body: A too-easy tempo leaves energy in the tank for the hold-up horses, with Party Dress and Jr Mahon able to reel in a fading front group in the dying strides; the long straight at Leopardstown gives closers enough time to close if the pace has been nothing more than a crawl.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest and the race becomes a test of stamina that bypasses the front and hold-up horses alike.
scenarios.body: A true staying gallop on Good ground can leave the front-runner empty and the hold-up horses with too much ground to make up, favouring horses who raced mid-to-prominent and had cover early; Jurality's strong recent form at this type of distance and consistent good-ground figures make him the prime candidate, with Tatum also well-suited.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is artificially slow early then sharp late, producing a sprint finish that theoretically suits deep closers.
scenarios.body: Miss Gitana and Folly Beach are the ostensible beneficiaries of a punishing late sprint, but both carry REDISTRIBUTED tags meaning they are not guaranteed their true hold-up position and their recent form offers limited confidence; Stone Rulya has faded in finishes and is similarly unreliable in this shape, making this the least likely winning scenario.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Trubshaw or Tatum apply any early pressure to Friary Road — if either pushes forward aggressively from the off, the pace quickens and hold-up horses get a better shot at closing.
Jr Mahon runs just three days after his last outing and should be monitored in the parade ring for any signs of fatigue or stiffness; a fresh horse in this shape it is not.

Miss Gitana and Folly Beach are both redistributed true hold-up types sitting in midfield on the map — if the pace is generous, they may drift back to their natural position and find themselves with too much ground to make up in the straight.

Stone Rulya's record of zero wins and zero places on turf in five outings is worth noting if the Good ground remains lively — any drying through the evening session would be the only angle that improves her profile here.
